newsitem.title: UK: UK grain markets locked in stalemate.
newsitem.headline: UK grain markets locked in stalemate.

text.p: UK grains markets remained locked in stalemate on Monday with rising futures on the back of a weaker sterling keeping many players sidelined.
"Just when you think the market can't get any worse, it does," said one broker.
Brokers said farmers were not willing to accept the lower prices while there was little real upside to the market owing to a lack of export business.

"People think the market will go lower, but they won't sell it short because the farmers won't move and there is very little upside to the market because there is no sign of any build up in export demand, so we have stalemate," said another broker.
No business was reported on the fob market.
"If you can find a market, buyers and sellers are about one stg apart," one broker said.
On the delivered market traded levels were little changed in minimal activity.
LIFFE wheat futures were 0.85 to 0.70 stg up, mainly on lower sterling, after trading 130 lots almost half of which were done during the last half an hour of trading.
LIFFE barley closed 0.25 stg to 0.55 stg higher after trading only 16 lots
